6237-the-lane-that-had-no-turning-volume.creator: Gilbert Parker
6237-the-lane-that-had-no-turning-volume.description: A book by Gilbert Parker. acter, as exhibited in the democratic yet monarchical province of Quebec, or Lower Canada (as, historically, I still love to think of it), moved by friendly observation, and seeking to be truthful and impartial, I have made this book and others dealing with the life of the proud province, which a century and a half of English governance has not Anglicised.

arxiv-2107-11765.title: Conditional Inference for Multivariate Generalised Linear Mixed Models
arxiv-2107-11765.creator: Jeanett S. Pelck, Rodrigo Labouriau
arxiv-2107-11765.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jeanett S. Pelck, Rodrigo Labouriau. We propose a method for inference in generalised linear mixed models (GLMMs) and several extensions of these models. First, we extend the GLMM by allowing the distribution of the random components to be non-Gaussian, that is, assuming an absolutely continuous distribution with respect to the Lebesgue measure that is symmetric around zero, unimodal and with finite moments up to fourth-order. Second, we allow the conditional distribution to follow a dispersion model instead of exponential dispersion models.

arxiv-2109-13862.title: 3N-GAN: Semi-Supervised Classification of X-Ray Images with a 3-Player Adversarial Framework
arxiv-2109-13862.creator: Shafin Haque, Ayaan Haque 0
arxiv-2109-13862.description: Abstract The success of deep learning for medical imaging tasks, such as classification, is heavily reliant on the availability of large-scale datasets. However, acquiring datasets with large quantities of labeled data is challenging, as labeling is expensive and time-consuming. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) is a growing alternative to fully-supervised learning, but requires unlabeled samples for training.

arxiv-2205-08289.title: Experiments on Generalizability of User-Oriented Fairness in Recommender Systems Conference: Proceedings of the 45th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval; July 11–15, 2022; Madrid, Spain Proceedings of the 45th International ACM SIGIR Conference on
arxiv-2205-08289.creator: Hossein A. Rahmani, Mohammadmehdi Naghiaei, Mahdi Dehghan, Mohammad Aliannejadi
arxiv-2205-08289.description: Abstract . Recent work in recommender systems mainly focuses on fairness in recommendations as an important aspect of measuring recommendations quality. A fairness-aware recommender system aims to treat different user groups similarly. Relevant work on user-oriented fairness highlights the discriminative behavior of fairness-unaware recommendation algorithms towards a certain user group, defined based on users’ activity level.

arxiv-2301-09742.title: Topological understanding of Neural Networks
arxiv-2301-09742.creator: Tushar Pandey
arxiv-2301-09742.description: Abstract In this review paper, we look at the internal structure of neural networks which is usually treated as a black box. The easiest and most comprehensible thing to do is to look at a binary classification and try to understand the approach a neural network takes.

arxiv-2306-15160.title: Study of Baryon Number Transport Dynamics and Strangeness Conservation Effects Using Ω \Omega -hadron Correlations
arxiv-2306-15160.creator: Weijie Dong 1, Xiaozhou Yu 1, Siyuan Ping 1, Xiatong Wu 2, Gang Wang 2, Huan Zhong Huang 1,2, Zi-Wei Lin 3
arxiv-2306-15160.description: Abstract In nuclear collisions at RHIC energies, an excess of Ω \Omega hyperons over Ω ¯ \overline{\Omega} is observed, indicating that Ω \Omega carries a net baryon number despite s s and s ¯ \bar{s} quarks being produced in pairs.

arxiv-2410-05116.title: HERO : H uman-Feedback- E fficient R einforcement Learning for O nline Diffusion Model Finetuning
arxiv-2410-05116.creator: Ayano Hiranaka Shang-Fu Chen Chieh-Hsin Lai, Dongjun Kim Naoki Murata Takashi Shibuya Wei-Hsiang Liao, Shao-Hua Sun Yuki Mitsufuji
arxiv-2410-05116.description: Abstract Controllable generation through Stable Diffusion (SD) fine-tuning aims to improve fidelity, safety, and alignment with human guidance. Existing reinforcement learning from human feedback methods usually rely on predefined heuristic reward functions or pretrained reward models built on large-scale datasets, limiting their applicability to scenarios where collecting such data is costly or difficult.

arxiv-2501-09393.title: SVIA: A Street View Image Anonymization Framework for Self-Driving Applications
arxiv-2501-09393.creator: Dongyu Liu, Xuhong Wang, Cen Chen, Yanhao Wang, Shengyue Yao, Yilun Lin
arxiv-2501-09393.description: Abstract In recent years, there has been an increasing interest in image anonymization, particularly focusing on the de-identification of faces and individuals. However, for self-driving applications, merely de-identifying faces and individuals might not provide sufficient privacy protection since street views like vehicles and buildings can still disclose locations, trajectories, and other sensitive information.

arxiv-2505-16519.title: SONIC: Cost-Effective Web Access for Developing Countries
arxiv-2505-16519.creator: Ayush Pandey, Rohail Asim, Jean Louis K. E. Fendji, Talal Rahwan, Matteo Varvello, Yasir Zaki
arxiv-2505-16519.description: Abstract Over 2.6 billion people remain without access to the Internet in 2025. This phenomenon is especially pronounced in developing regions, where cost and infrastructure limitations are major barriers to connectivity. In response, we design SONIC, a low-cost, scalable data delivery system that builds on existing infrastructures: FM radio for downlink broadcasting, and SMS for personalized uplink.

arxiv-2505-20033.title: EmoNet-Face : An Expert-Annotated Benchmark for Synthetic Emotion Recognition
arxiv-2505-20033.creator: Christoph Schuhmann, Robert Kaczmarczyk, Gollam Rabby, Felix Friedrich, Maurice Kraus, Krishna Kalyan, Kourosh Nadi, Huu Nguyen, Kristian Kersting, Sören Auer
arxiv-2505-20033.description: Abstract Effective human-AI interaction relies on AI’s ability to accurately perceive and interpret human emotions. Current benchmarks for vision and vision-language models are severely limited, offering a narrow emotional spectrum that overlooks nuanced states (e.g., bitterness, intoxication) and fails to distinguish subtle differences between related feelings (e.g., shame vs. embarrassment).

arxiv-2512-17196.title: UmniBench: Unified Understanding and Generation Model Oriented Omni-dimensional Benchmark
arxiv-2512-17196.creator: Kai Liu, Leyang Chen, Wenbo Li, Zhikai Chen, Zhixin Wang, Renjing Pei, Linghe Kong, Yulun Zhang
arxiv-2512-17196.description: Abstract Unifying multimodal understanding and generation has shown impressive capabilities in cutting-edge proprietary systems. However, evaluations of unified multimodal models (UMMs) remain decoupled, assessing their understanding and generation abilities separately with corresponding datasets. To address this, we propose UmniBench, a benchmark tailored for UMMs with omni-dimensional evaluation.

pmc-11422030.title: Topic: Returns to education in Ghana: The role of education of one's father
pmc-11422030.creator: Emmanuel AduBoahen, Paul Hammond, Paul A Kwakwa
pmc-11422030.description: The study examines the role of education of father on returns to schooling in Ghana. The data used for the analysis is the Ghana Living Standards Survey Seven (GLSS 7). Spouse education is used as an instrument in our estimation. Father's education, other demographic characteristics and employment characteristics were controlled in the study.

pmc-11464821.title: Patient Caregiver Perspectives on Accessing Language Interpretation in a Pediatric Emergency Department
pmc-11464821.creator: Emily A. Hartford, Nicholas Dimenstein, Dwight Barry, K. Casey Lion
pmc-11464821.description: Patients and caregivers with a language for care other than English (LOE) are at risk for inequitable care in the pediatric emergency department (ED). Professional interpretation (PI) improves outcomes, but there can be complexity in determining optimal language for care and interpretation need.

pmc-11475265.title: Arsenic in Rice and Rice-Based Products with Regard to Consumer Health
pmc-11475265.creator: Monika Rajkowska-Myśliwiec, Artur Ciemniak, Gabriela Karp, Cristina Couto, Elisa Keating
pmc-11475265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Most articles on the exposure to arsenic (As) associated with rice and rice products come from Asia where these products are consumed in the largest quantities; relatively few of the articles have focused on European consumers. Since rice products can represent a significant contribution to overall arsenic exposure, the aim of the study was to determine the total arsenic content (tAs) in rice and the most commonly-consumed rice products available on the Polish market.

pmc-11490105.title: Evaluating the efficacy of support groups in the metaverse for Ukrainian refugees: a protocol for a randomized clinical trial
pmc-11490105.creator: Cezar Giosan, Cătălina-Maria Popoviciu, Saltanat Zhamaliyeva, Iuliana Zaborot, George Deac
pmc-11490105.description: BackgroundThe Ukrainian crisis, sparked by the Russian invasion, has generated one of the most extensive refugee crises in modern history. Addressing the mental health challenges of Ukrainian refugees is critical to promoting their resilience and successful integration into host communities.

pmc-11550201.title: Otostegia fruticosa (Forssk.) – A comprehensive insight of its ethnopharmacology, phytochemistry, and pharmacological activities
pmc-11550201.creator: Mohammed F Hawwal, Sarfaraz Ahmed, Perwez Alam, Omer I Fantoukh, Gadah A AlHamoud, Hattan A Alharbi, Waleed A Alobaid, Hanan Khojah
pmc-11550201.description: Otostegia fruticosa (Forssk.) is a shrub of the Lamiaceae family with a wide geographic distribution in Saudi Arabia, Western and Eastern Africa, Ethiopia, and the Middle East. The current study provides an overview of recent developments in the knowledge of O. fruticosa’s ethnobotanical, pharmacological, and phytochemical properties.

pmc-11671212.title: Caregiving in Asia: Priority areas for research, policy, and practice to support family caregivers
pmc-11671212.creator: Nan Jiang, Bei Wu, Yan Li
pmc-11671212.description: Population aging presents a growing societal challenge and imposes a heavy burden on the healthcare system in many Asian countries. Given the limited availability of formal long‐term care (LTC) facilities and personnel, family caregivers play a vital role in providing care for the increasing population of older adults.

pmc-11689178.title: INTERGENERATIONAL HEALTH PROMOTION PROJECT TO REDUCE OLDER ADULT SOCIAL ISOLATION AND LONELINESS: A FEASIBILITY STUDY
pmc-11689178.creator: Jeremy Holloway
pmc-11689178.description: Emerging research demonstrates that social isolation and loneliness are linked to significant physical and mental health conditions. To address these concerns, the Tellegacy program was developed as an intergenerational health-promoting intervention to ameliorate older adult social isolation and loneliness in an effort to increase wellness.

pmc-13052556.title: Quality appraisal of clinical guidelines for newborns in China: a systematic review protocol
pmc-13052556.creator: Li Jing, Zengzhen Liao, Luqin Liao, Xuejun Zhai, Mingfen Tang, Qiong Bin
pmc-13052556.description: AbstractIntroductionNeonatal guidelines are critical for enhancing healthcare quality and reducing neonatal mortality in China. However, the methodological quality of existing guidelines varies considerably, and the credibility and implementability (CI) of their recommendations has not been systematically evaluated. Consequently, key areas for improvement remain unclear.

pmc-13556876.title: 796. Basal cortisol levels across the menstrual cycle in premenstrual dysphoric disorder and premenstrual syndrome: A systematic review and meta-analysis evaluating methodological heterogeneity
pmc-13556876.creator: P-H Chen, P-J Chen
pmc-13556876.description: BackgroundPremenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) and premenstrual syndrome (PMS) are characterized by cyclical affective and somatic symptoms. The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis has been extensively investigated as a potential biological substrate for these conditions. However, the existing literature regarding basal cortisol levels remains highly inconsistent.

pmc-13585803.title: Evaluating the feasibility and safety of 48-h short-stay pathway for robot-assisted laparoscopic partial nephrectomy: a propensity score-matched analysis
pmc-13585803.creator: Caihong Tang, Ningping Chu, Chenghao Shi, Zhongwen Chang, Taoyue Zhao, Hong He, Yiman Zhang, Lingling Jing
pmc-13585803.description: ObjectiveTo compare perioperative outcomes between the 48-h short-stay pathway and traditional inpatient management for patients undergoing robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), and to evaluate the feasibility, safety, recovery efficiency, and economic benefits of the 48-h short-stay pathway.MethodsThis retrospective study included 175 patients who underwent RAPN between February 2022 and June 2024.

uslaw-usc-t21-s392.title: 21 U.S.C. § 392 — Exemption of meats and meat food products
uslaw-usc-t21-s392.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t21-s392.description: United States Code, Title 21 (Food And Drugs); Chapter 9 (Federal Food, Drug, And Cosmetic Act); Subchapter X (Miscellaneous). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Law determinative of exemption Meats and meat food products shall be exempt from the provisions of this chapter to the extent of the application or the extension thereto of the Meat Inspection Act, approved March 4, 1907.
